chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan and more than one other, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — has ordained for the poor, within the wealth of the rich, what is sufficient for them; and had it not been for that, He would have increased it further for them. Rather, they are impoverished due to the withholding of those who withheld it from them.

key_terms.الأغنياء: The wealthy/rich — those with surplus wealth above their needs, upon whom zakat obligations fall
key_terms.الفقراء: The poor — those lacking sufficient wealth for their needs; the primary recipients of zakat
key_terms.ما يكفيهم: What suffices/is sufficient for them — denotes a divinely ordained threshold of need
key_terms.منع: Withholding, denial — the act of refusing to give what is divinely owed; the theological cause of poverty

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the rights of the poor in the wealth of the rich?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that God Almighty has divinely ordained a sufficient share for the poor within the wealth of the rich — and had the rich withheld even more, God would have ordained an even greater share. The poverty of the poor, then, is not a divine abandonment but a direct consequence of the rich failing to fulfill their God-given obligation. This teaching establishes the theological basis for zakat and khums as divine rights embedded in wealth, not merely charitable acts.
word_analysis: He would have increased it for them

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ibn Muskan and someone else,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made for the poor, in the wealth of the rich, what would suffice them, and had it not been that, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Increased it for them, and rather they are poor due to the prevention of the ones who prevented it from them’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ibn Muskan and more than one person who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has assigned in properties of affluent people a share for the needy that is sufficient to meet their need; otherwise, He would have increased such share. Shortages come from non-payment of those who do not pay.”
